text:
The Pothole Is Not an Accident

On the morning of Saturday, 13 June 2026, a woman named Kantha was riding her two-wheeler along the Siddapur road near Marathahalli, dropping her daughter Neha at college. It had rained heavily the night before, and the potholes had filled with water, which is the detail that makes them invisible. She hit one, lost control and fell. A school bus coming from behind ran her over. She died on the road, in front of her daughter.

A case was registered at the Whitefield traffic police station. Against the bus.

That is the whole architecture of the problem in one line. There is always a vehicle to charge. There is never a road to charge.

Kantha's death was not a freak event. In Bengaluru it is closer to a season. The National Crime Records Bureau counts deaths caused by the negligence of civic bodies, meaning bad roads, potholes, open drains, collapsing infrastructure, electrocution. Bengaluru has ranked first among Indian metros in that category for six consecutive years. Delhi, bigger and denser and not famous for good roads, recorded four in a year when Bengaluru recorded seventeen. Either Bengaluru's roads are uniquely lethal, or every other city is better at not counting.

The national picture, in passing: figures tabled in Parliament record 9,438 people killed in pothole crashes between 2020 and 2024, about five a day, the toll rising 53% across those years. The Supreme Court called such numbers frightening as far back as 2018. Yet the same table shows Andhra Pradesh, Bihar and Goa reporting zero pothole deaths in five years. Not zero potholes. Zero deaths. That is not a measurement. It is a filing decision.

A pothole death exists, legally, only if a police officer writes the word pothole into an FIR. Most do not. The crash becomes rash driving, or a hit-and-run. There is a driver to arrest and a section of the penal code that fits him. There is no section that fits an engineer who certified a road that dissolved in the first monsoon.

Bengaluru has a case that shows exactly how that works. On 6 February 2021, Tasdeeq Bushra, nineteen and in her first year of MBBS, was riding home along Hennur Main Road. She swerved to avoid a pothole. A truck hit her scooter from behind, she fell, and she went under the wheels.

The truck belonged to the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike. The city's own civic body owned the vehicle that killed her, and the road, and the pothole she was avoiding. The driver was arrested under Section 304A, causing death by negligence. The agency was not. Her father, Mushtaq Ahmed, put it better than any court has: "We have lost our only child. Whom will we pin the blame on? The vehicle was BBMP's and so was the driver, the roads were poorly built by them." BBMP, the water board and the electricity utility then blamed one another, which is the standard procedure.

Two details from what followed are worth sitting with. The FIR did not mention the pothole. And the pothole was filled within hours of her death. The evidence was repaired faster than the case was built.

Hers is not an outlier, it is the template. The News Minute traced thirteen pothole deaths in Bengaluru between 2017 and 2022. Families compensated: zero. Officials held accountable: zero. Not for want of a policy. BBMP had notified one, three lakh rupees for a death, and reporters found zonal chief engineers who did not know it existed and had never received a claim. A right nobody is told about is not a right, it is a press release. When Ashwin, twenty-seven, died on a pothole in MS Palya, police first blamed him for riding irresponsibly. His mother fought to get one line into the FIR naming unnamed civic officers. Nothing came of it.

The courts have been trying for a decade. A petition filed in 2015 is still running, and the High Court has reprimanded the corporation repeatedly, once issuing a contempt notice after BBMP resisted paying compensation at all. At one hearing, BBMP informed the court that Bengaluru contained 221 potholes in total. The court told it to be honest.

Then came the deadline. After a student named Dhanushree was crushed by a tipper lorry in September 2025 while swerving around a pothole, the Chief Minister announced that Bengaluru would be pothole-free by the end of October, with eleven hundred crore rupees sanctioned. Officials counted potholes by the thousand and announced them filled. The deadline was missed and replaced with another. In Whitefield, residents watched gravel tipped into holes, gravel that scatters as soon as vehicles pass over it.

Here is how that pothole-free year ended. On 20 November, three weeks after the deadline, Shantamma, forty-six, riding pillion home from work, fell on a broken stretch in Hulimavu and was run over by a truck. Police blamed potholes and loose gravel. On 17 December, Tabrez, thirty-two, swerved near Nelamangala and put his front wheel into an unbarricaded pipeline pit. He died at NIMHANS two days later. Not a pothole, strictly. The same disease.

Then the rains came back in June, and so did the holes, and so did Kantha's funeral.

The exhausting part is that the effort is real. The money is spent, the holes are counted and announced, and they return on schedule, because filling a pothole is not building a road. A pothole is the visible end of a chain: a specification diluted, a layer skipped, a bill cleared, an inspection signed. Every hole in a Bengaluru road has a name attached to it somewhere. None of those names ever reaches an FIR.

A drunk driver goes to jail. A negligent engineer gets transferred. A contractor whose road failed in ten weeks bids for the next tender. The person who dies becomes a line in a table.

Bengaluru has led that table for six years and has still not produced one official who lost a job over a death. Until a road failure is something a person can be charged with, the ritual continues: a monsoon, a hole, a two-wheeler, a bus behind it, a case against the driver, gravel by the weekend, and a family being told that what happened to them was an accident.

It was not an accident. Someone built that.

urgent attention serious information received from credible sources regarding the functioning and activities of an establishment operating under the name and style of “Wave Wellness Spa”, situated within the territorial jurisdiction of Kandivali Police Station, Mumbai.

The information received raises serious concerns regarding the alleged use of the said establishment for prostitution, commercial sexual exploitation, trafficking-related activities and other illicit sexual activities, under the guise of a wellness/massage spa.

In view of the seriousness of the information, I respectfully request that the allegations be independently verified through a discreet, fair and impartial investigation, preferably with the involvement of the Anti-Human Trafficking Unit / Crime Branch, so that the actual nature of activities being carried out at the premises can be ascertained.

1. INFORMATION REQUIRING INVESTIGATION

It has been reported to me from credible sources that the establishment may be functioning as a front for prostitution and other unlawful activities.

It is specifically alleged that:

Women and young adult female workers are allegedly being brought or engaged at the premises for the purpose of providing sexual services to customers in exchange for money.
Information received further indicates that some of the women allegedly working at the establishment may be from Bangladesh, Nepal and the North-Eastern States of India. This information requires careful verification of their identity, nationality, residential status, employment particulars and the circumstances in which they came to work at the establishment.
There are allegations that the owner/operator of the establishment, Mr. Pawan Kumar, is directly or indirectly involved in the operation and management of the premises and may have knowledge of, or participation in, the alleged activities.
It is further alleged that the establishment may be facilitating or permitting commercial sexual activities, prostitution or sexual exploitation under the appearance of providing massage/wellness services.
The police may kindly investigate whether any person is procuring, inducing, recruiting, transporting, harbouring, controlling or otherwise facilitating the exploitation of women for prostitution or commercial sexual activities.
It may also kindly be verified whether any woman working at the establishment has been subjected to coercion, deception, threats, financial exploitation, confinement, withholding of identity documents or any other form of exploitation.
The establishment is reportedly situated in close proximity to a Police Beat Office and active Beat Staff. This circumstance may also kindly be examined independently to ascertain whether previous complaints, information, inspections or preventive action concerning the establishment have been recorded.

I respectfully clarify that the above allegations are being placed before the police for investigation and verification and not as established findings of fact. I request that no person be treated as guilty unless the allegations are established through lawful investigation and evidence.

2. VERIFICATION OF LICENCES AND PERMISSIONS

The competent authorities may kindly verify whether “Wave Wellness Spa” possesses all licences, registrations and permissions legally applicable to its actual activities, including:

MCGM trade/business permissions;
Shops and Establishments registration, wherever applicable;
Police permissions/NOC, if legally required for the particular activity;
Health and sanitation permissions, wherever applicable;
Fire and safety permissions, wherever applicable;
details of the proprietor/owner/operator;
details of the actual person conducting and controlling the business; and
the permitted nature of activities at the premises.

If the establishment is found to be operating beyond the scope of its permissions, appropriate action may kindly be initiated by the competent authority.

3. INVESTIGATION REGARDING POSSIBLE PROSTITUTION / TRAFFICKING

The police may kindly investigate whether offences under the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956 (ITP Act) or any other applicable law are disclosed.

The ITP Act specifically contains provisions concerning keeping or managing a brothel or allowing premises to be used as a brothel under Section 3, prostitution in or in the vicinity of specified public places under Section 7, and procuring/inducing/taking a person for prostitution under Section 5. The Act also provides statutory procedures concerning search and investigation, including Section 15.

The investigating authorities may therefore kindly ascertain, based upon evidence, whether any offence under the ITP Act or other applicable criminal law has occurred.

4. REQUEST FOR DISCREET CROSS-VERIFICATION

Considering the nature of the allegations, I respectfully request that the matter be cross-verified by an independent police team / Crime Branch / Anti-Human Trafficking Unit, rather than relying solely upon a routine verification by the local beat staff.

The investigating team may kindly examine:

The identity and particulars of the proprietor/operator, including Mr. Pawan Kumar, if he is found to be the person controlling the establishment.
The identity and employment particulars of all persons working at the establishment.
The circumstances under which women from different States or countries, if any, have been recruited or brought to the premises.
Whether any foreign nationals are present or employed and, if so, whether their immigration, visa, passport and other legally required documents are valid.
Whether any person has been brought to Mumbai through agents, intermediaries or other persons for employment at the establishment.
Whether any money is being collected from customers for sexual services.
Whether the owner/operator or any intermediary receives commissions or other financial benefits from such activities.
Whether there is any evidence of trafficking, coercion, inducement, exploitation or forced prostitution.
Whether there are links between the establishment and any other spa, massage centre, hotel, lodge or premises where similar activities may allegedly be taking place.
5. PRESERVATION AND EXAMINATION OF EVIDENCE

I further request that, wherever legally permissible, the investigating agency take immediate steps for the preservation and lawful collection of relevant evidence, including:

CCTV recordings;
visitor/customer registers;
appointment records;
employee/staff registers;
attendance records;
payment records;
digital booking records;
mobile-phone or electronic evidence where legally authorised;
advertisements and online listings;
relevant bank/payment transaction records; and
other documentary or electronic evidence relevant to determining the actual nature of the activities.

Any search, seizure or examination of electronic evidence may kindly be conducted strictly in accordance with the applicable statutory procedure and evidentiary safeguards.

6. REGISTRATION OF FIR IF COGNIZABLE OFFENCE IS DISCLOSED

Under Section 173 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS), information relating to the commission of a cognizable offence may be given to the officer in charge of a police station. The provision also sets out the procedure concerning such information and investigation.

Accordingly, if the verification/investigation discloses a cognizable offence, I respectfully request that an FIR be registered under the appropriate provisions of the ITP Act, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 and/or any other applicable law, and that a proper investigation be conducted.

7. REQUEST FOR ACTION AGAINST THE OWNER/OPERATOR IF EVIDENCE IS FOUND

If investigation establishes the involvement of Mr. Pawan Kumar, the proprietor/operator or any other person, appropriate criminal and regulatory action may kindly be taken against the person/persons found responsible.

The investigation may specifically determine whether the owner/operator:

knowingly permitted the premises to be used for prostitution;
financially benefited from prostitution;
recruited or procured women for prostitution;
facilitated trafficking or commercial sexual exploitation;
knowingly harboured or controlled persons for such activities; or
violated applicable licensing and regulatory requirements.

Any action may kindly be taken only on the basis of evidence and in accordance with law.

8. REQUEST FOR APPROPRIATE PROTECTION OF POTENTIAL VICTIMS

If during the investigation any woman is found to be a victim of trafficking, coercion, exploitation or any other offence, I respectfully request that she be treated as a potential victim and not merely as an accused, and that appropriate protection, medical assistance, counselling and other legally prescribed assistance be provided.

Dear @raghav_chadha ,

I know you are doing very well in Parliament by raising small issues that were ignored by most Members of Parliament but have a bigger impact.

I am writing this post regarding an account lien and bank freeze by the Cyber Police of India.

In my case, the issue started when I received a message from my bank branch stating that my account had received a police notice of lien of 6000 rupees. I immediately went to my bank branch and asked them why my account had a lien of 6000 rupees. They followed some procedure and gave me a printout which contained the acknowledgement of my lien. One of the bank employees told me that I should contact the cyber police mentioned on the paper and provide them with the details of the 6000 rupees, such as where it came from and for what reason. However, they did not give me any specific reason why my bank account had received the lien.

Later, I checked my bank statement to find the details of the 6000 rupees transaction and noticed that my case was reported on 6 December 2025, and I had received a transaction of 6000 rupees on the same date. I remember that my neighbour had sent me this 6000 rupees and asked me to withdraw it from the ATM because he had an urgent situation as his mother was going to her village due to an emergency. As a friend, I withdrew the money and gave it to him.

Now I have all the proofs and details to explain to the police, so I emailed all the details to the Bangalore Cyber Cell or the police station where my notice was issued, as mentioned in the acknowledgement given by my bank. However, I did not receive any response. I then tried to contact the investigation officer mentioned in the report. I called several times, keeping a gap of five to six hours out of respect for his time and duties, as they may have many other responsibilities. I also sent him a message on WhatsApp, but there was still no response.

After four to five days, I called again, and this time he picked up the call. He was speaking in the local language, which I did not understand, as I am from Maharashtra and not familiar with the local language of Bangalore. I then started speaking in English, and he told me that I have to come to Bangalore and verify my documents. I explained that for 6000 rupees, it would not be beneficial for me to travel to Bangalore because transportation, food, and stay would cost more than 6000 rupees. He said that he does not know and that I have to come, otherwise he will not issue the No Objection Certificate, and then he ended the call.

This issue may look small, but similar issues are happening everywhere, and no one is noticing them. It feels like “Kare koi aur bhare koi.” Many innocent people face this issue, and it remains unresolved. Because of chain transactions that come into accounts, some people are unable to use their own money. If I travel, I will have to spend more than 6000 rupees to remove the lien. I believe this issue can be resolved through email or online verification, but the investigation officer denied it.

I am also tagging Pushpendra Sir @pushpendrakum and Bangalore Cyber Police @BlrCityPolice . If you could please look into this matter.

Thank you.

Bhai aur beheno, agar aap bhi Binance P2P trading karte ho aur suddenly bank account freeze ho gaya hai toh pareshan mat ho. Yeh bahut common problem hai India mein. Innocent log bhi fas jaate hain jab kisi buyer/seller ka paisa kisi fraud case se link hota hai.

Yeh steps follow karo - 

1️⃣ Sabse Pehle Bank Branch Jaao  
   - Freeze ka exact reason, Cyber Crime complaint number, IO naam aur Police Station details lo.  
   - Written notice maang lo.

2️⃣ Saare Proofs Collect Karo (Bahut Important)  
   - Binance P2P complete order history (screenshots)  
   - Buyer/Seller ke saath chat  
   - Payment proof (UPI, bank transfer screenshot)  
   - Bank statement jisme transaction dikhe  
   - Aadhaar, PAN, Binance account details

3️⃣ Binance Support ko turant contact karo  
   - App mein Help section → Submit ticket  
   - Order ID aur proofs attach karo. Woh counterparty ko investigate kar sakte hain.

4️⃣ Cyber Cell mein Representation Daalo  
   - Local Cyber Police Station ya online portal pe jaao.  
   - Detailed application likho ki transaction genuine tha Binance P2P pe hua.  
   - Saare proofs attach karo.  
   - Lawyer (Cyber crime specialist) ki madad le lo - yeh bahut kaam aata hai.

• P2P ke liye alag dedicated bank account use karo (savings account mat use karo)

Statement on restrictions faced by cartoonists Satish Acharya and Manjul on Instagram

https://t.co/X7ipfsWjp2 strongly condemns the restrictions faced by cartoonists @satishacharya and @MANJULtoons on Instagram. On 26th September, Manjul’s cartoon on the Election Commission was restricted in India “pursuant to a notice from the Government of India/Law Enforcement.” 

Satish Acharya also repeatedly faced takedowns of his posts on Instagram, and on 28th September, his account got restricted in India. The notification shared by the cartoonist stated that the platform had to “repeatedly restrict access to content posted” by him “pursuant to legal requirements.”

In March 2026, Satish also received two notifications from @X stating that @GoI_MeitY had ordered the platform to block his content. He also received a notification from X about a content takedown request from the Cyber Crime Department of the Mumbai Police. These cartoons depicted India’s stance on US-Israel bombing on Iran and the killing of its supreme leader. Another cartoon showed the arms of state actors forming a human chain around billionaire Gautam Adani with the caption “Ek hain to safe hain.”

These notifications also stated that the platform could not provide him with additional information due to legal restrictions. This lack of transparency makes it particularly difficult to challenge a blocking order. While notifications issued by X identified the authorities that ordered the takedowns, Instagram did not disclose which authorities had ordered the takedowns. In such instances, before a creator can even consider approaching a court, they may first have to determine which government authority issued the order, under what legal provision it was issued, and what specific content or reasoning formed the basis for it. Without access to this information, exercising the right to challenge the restriction becomes significantly harder. 

Even when the information is available, going to court requires time, money, and legal assistance. All of these resources may not even be available for cartoonists, independent creators, or students. For someone facing multiple takedown orders, challenging each restriction individually can become an exhausting and expensive exercise.

@scroll_in’s article on the restrictions faced by Satish Acharya stated that the cartoonist attempted to challenge Meta’s action but was unable to reach Instagram’s help centre due to its automated grievance redressal systems and the lack of access to human support. Meta’s AI Support Assistant provides ‘In-App Appeal’ as the ‘primary method for challenging a content decision.’ However, this method is not a statutory remedy, amenable to further challenge at the Grievance Appellate Committee level. The prescribed procedure of approaching the Grievance Officer through Meta’s official reporting form does not provide a method to report the takedown of content, either for violations of Meta Community Standards, Terms of Service, or takedowns through “automated systems implemented under legal requirements.”

https://t.co/X7ipfsWjp2 has also observed that the Grievance Officer email address available on the website can only be used to enquire about the grievance redressal mechanism and not to file a Grievance Officer report. This also creates a structural barrier to access further remedies, such as approaching the Grievance Appellate Committee, which mandatorily requires a Grievance Officer report to be filed prior to filing an appeal.

In the past few months, https://t.co/X7ipfsWjp2 has recorded similar instances of restrictions faced by other cartoonists in India. In August 2026, @cartoonistrrs's posts showing a comical representation of the PM’s viral reel received a takedown notice, and @cartoonistvish faced 4 takedown orders for his cartoon criticising Prime Minister Narender Modi’s foreign travels during domestic issues. Even a simple satire by @BagchiAsh, showing the PM with a Melody chocolate on his forehead, was restricted on Meta.

Over time, such instances of censorship can have consequences far beyond individual takedowns. When creators repeatedly see their work removed without clear explanations and realise that the only meaningful way to challenge the decision may be through costly legal proceedings, they may begin to censor themselves. The uncertainty surrounding what can be taken down and the difficulty of fighting back when takedowns happen can eventually discourage people from creating altogether. If the cost of speaking becomes too high and the consequences too unpredictable, creators may censor themselves or give up on their art entirely.

The increasing trend of censorship of cartoons and political humour is deeply concerning, particularly because it points to a shrinking space for dissent in India. The right to freedom of speech and expression is a fundamental right, and the ability to question, criticise and even ridicule those in power is an essential part of a democratic society. Dissent may be uncomfortable for governments, but discomfort cannot be the basis for silencing it.

The Government should also ensure that the users are provided with meaningful, accessible, and timely avenues for content takedowns and account restrictions.

Statement: IFF condemns the internet shutdown in Connaught Place ahead of today's protest. We are tracing the suspension order.

New Delhi, 2 October 2026

The Internet Freedom Foundation (IFF) condemns the suspension of mobile internet services in and around Connaught Place, New Delhi, this morning. At 9:40 am, Jio subscribers in the area received a message stating: "As per government instructions Internet services have been stopped in your area till further notice." The shutdown took effect before a protest called for 11 am at Jantar Mantar, seeking the resignation of the Chief Election Commissioner, had even begun. 

Delhi Police has refused permission for the gathering, prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 are in force across New Delhi district, and entry and exit at eleven metro stations have been closed. On Gandhi Jayanti, the answer to a call for protest in the capital has been to switch off the internet for everyone who lives, works, trades and reports in its centre. We call for the immediate restoration of services. 

At the time of release of this statement, we have not been able to locate any suspension order published by the Ministry of Home Affairs, the Department of Telecommunications, the Government of NCT of Delhi or the Delhi Police. The public does not know who directed this shutdown, on what grounds, over what area, or until when. IFF is attempting to trace the order and will make it public as soon as we obtain a copy.

In Anuradha Bhasin v. Union of India, (2020) 3 SCC 637, the Supreme Court held that speech and trade over the internet are protected under Articles 19(1)(a) and 19(1)(g) of the Constitution, and that every suspension order must be published, reasoned, proportionate and limited in time. Under Section 20(2)(b) of the Telecommunications Act, 2023 and the Telecommunications (Temporary Suspension of Services) Rules, 2024, only the Union or State Home Secretary may issue such an order, for reasons recorded in writing. The order must be published and must specify the area, the services and a fixed duration and it may be passed only where no other reasonable means would serve. A shutdown announced to subscribers as lasting "till further notice", imposed before a single person had assembled, cannot be squared with these safeguards. It follows repeated suspensions around Jantar Mantar in July 2026. Switching off the network is becoming a routine response to protest in the national capital. IFF condemns the internet shutdown in parts of Central Delhi. 

We call upon the Government of India and the Government of NCT of Delhi to:

1. Immediately restore mobile internet services in Connaught Place and all affected parts of Central Delhi.

2. Publish the suspension order forthwith, together with the reasons recorded in writing.

3. Disclose the issuing authority, the precise areas and services covered, and the period of operation.

4. Place the order before the Review Committee within five days, as the Rules require, and make its findings public.
